starting_principles: Global conservation of energy for an isolated system: $\Delta E_{\text{universe}} = 0$
Partition of system energy: $E_{\text{system}} = E_{\text{macro}} + U$
Mechanical boundary work for a quasi-static expansion: $dW = P dV$
Equivalence of mechanical work and thermal energy transfer (Joule's principle)
assumptions: The thermodynamic system is closed (no mass transfer across system boundaries).
Macroscopic kinetic and potential energies of the system as a whole are constant ($dE_{\text{macro}} = 0$).
Thermodynamic states are well-defined equilibrium states.

ordered_steps.description: Formulate the universal conservation of energy for the isolated composite system comprising the thermodynamic system and its surroundings.
ordered_steps.operation: Express the conservation principle in differential form: $dE_{\text{system}} + dE_{\text{surroundings}} = 0$.
assumptions_applied: Combined universe (system + surroundings) is an isolated system.

ordered_steps.description: Partition system energy into macroscopic mechanical energy and microscopic internal energy $U$.
ordered_steps.operation: Set macroscopic mechanical energy variations to zero ($dK_{\text{macro}} = 0$, $d\Phi_{\text{macro}} = 0$) for a stationary system at rest in the laboratory frame: $dE_{\text{system}} = dU$.
assumptions_applied: The system center of mass is stationary with zero macroscopic acceleration.

ordered_steps.description: Classify boundary energy transfers into mechanical work $dW$ performed by the system and heat $dQ$ absorbed by the system.
ordered_steps.operation: By definition of energy conservation at the boundary, energy gained by surroundings consists of mechanical work done on them ($+dW$) minus thermal energy transferred from them into the system ($-dQ$): $-dE_{\text{surroundings}} = dQ - dW$.
assumptions_applied: Energy crossing the boundary occurs exclusively via mechanical work and heat conduction/radiation.

ordered_steps.description: Equate the internal energy change $dU$ to the net boundary energy transfer.
ordered_steps.operation: Substitute $-dE_{\text{surroundings}} = dQ - dW$ into the energy balance: $dU = dQ - dW$.
assumptions_applied: Physics sign convention: $dQ$ into system is positive, $dW$ by system is positive.

ordered_steps.description: Express mechanical boundary work in terms of pressure and volume change for a quasi-static process.
ordered_steps.operation: For an outward displacement $dx$ of a piston of cross-sectional area $A$ against internal pressure $P$: $dW = (P A) dx = P (A dx) = P dV$.
assumptions_applied: Quasi-static boundary displacement without turbulence or viscous shock.

ordered_steps.description: Combine expressions to write the differential First Law with state and path distinctions.
ordered_steps.operation: Substitute $dW = P dV$: $dQ = dU + P dV$. Note that $dU$ is an exact differential of state ($\oint dU = 0$), whereas $dQ$ and $dW$ are inexact path-dependent differentials.
assumptions_applied: Internal energy $U$ is a single-valued state function.

applicability_conditions: Valid for all closed thermodynamic systems.
Sign convention: $dQ > 0$ for heat absorbed by the system, $dW > 0$ for work performed by the system.
Valid for reversible and irreversible processes (with $dW = P dV$ applying strictly in quasi-static conditions).
